routes.description: Establish the core historical facts, defend their evidential basis, and show that resurrection explains them better than the principal skeptical alternatives within a theistic context.
routes.successCriteria: The resurrection must remain the strongest overall explanation after accounting for its prior probability, the reliability of the historical premises, and competing naturalistic accounts.

motionBridge.description: Connect the established historical facts to resurrection as their best overall explanation under ordinary historical comparison.

centralBridges.description: Establish the crucifixion, burial, empty tomb, postmortem experiences, and transformed disciples as the relevant historical data.
Show that resurrection has greater explanatory power and scope than conspiracy, hallucination, and legendary-development accounts.
Supply an independently supported theistic context in which divine resurrection is not intrinsically implausible.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Clarify that historical proof is probabilistic and depends on comparative evidential likelihood rather than mathematical demonstration.
Ground the appearance reports in early and independent traditions rather than solely in the dates of the completed Gospels.

routes.description: Prevent the resurrection inference by challenging its evidential standard, prior probability, historical premises, and claimed superiority over naturalistic or developmental alternatives.
routes.successCriteria: Reasonable evidential caution must remain warranted if the resurrection has an unfavorable prior, the underlying reports are uncertain, or naturalistic development can explain the record.

motionBridge.description: Show that the surrounding historical claims do not warrant resurrection as the best explanation when priors and evidential uncertainty are included.

centralBridges.description: Require evidence proportionate to the extraordinary character, significance, and asserted divine purpose of the resurrection claim.
Preserve sincere mistake, psychological experience, or other naturalistic possibilities as competitors to divine resurrection.
Challenge whether the appearance reports and other asserted facts are sufficiently early, independent, and reliable for the explanatory inference.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Distinguish establishing surrounding historical facts from inferring a supernatural event as their explanation.
Account for increasingly elaborate appearance narratives through development across the Gospel sequence.

sections.title: Historical proof and evidential standard
sections.rationale: The motion depends on what probabilistic historical inquiry can establish and whether the resurrection's extraordinary character changes the evidence required for the inference.

sections.title: Comparative prior probability
sections.rationale: The relative plausibility of divine intervention and imperfect naturalistic alternatives determines how the historical evidence bears on the competing explanations.

sections.title: Historical data and report reliability
sections.rationale: The explanatory comparison requires identifying which burial, tomb, appearance, and disciple-transformation claims are sufficiently established to demand explanation.

sections.title: Conspiracy and hallucination alternatives
sections.rationale: The motion requires comparing resurrection with accounts that preserve disciple sincerity while explaining their convictions or the relevant reports without divine intervention.

sections.title: Early tradition and legendary development
sections.rationale: The chronology and independence of the underlying traditions matter to whether the appearance narratives preserve early testimony or reflect later elaboration.
